drhp.business: Golkunda Diamonds & Jewellery Limited manufactures studded jewellery and deals in cut & polished diamonds, precious and semi-precious stones, primarily for export to long-standing retail-chain customers in Europe and the Middle East. It is now setting up a domestic manufacturing facility to supply fine jewellery to organised retail chains across major Indian cities.

risks.note: The United States is one of the largest export destinations for India's gems & jewellery industry; any increase in US import duties, tariff barriers or bilateral trade policy changes may hurt export competitiveness, pricing and volumes.

Escalating US-Iran-Israel tensions and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war may raise gold price volatility, logistics/freight costs, disrupt shipping routes and cause forex fluctuations, impacting global trade and business sentiment.
Fluctuations in gold, diamond and other precious metal prices can impact input costs and operating margins.
As an export-oriented business, foreign exchange rate fluctuations could affect export realisations and overall profitability.

Business is significantly oriented toward exports (to Europe, Middle East and the US); dependence on export markets is a structural concentration the Company is now seeking to reduce via domestic expansion.
Intensifying competition from domestic and international jewellery manufacturers may lead to pricing and margin pressures.
Changes in consumer spending patterns for luxury products, and discretionary spending pressure from gold price fluctuations and economic uncertainty, can affect demand.

Board-level risk management identifies raw material price risk, financial risk and foreign currency risk as key risks monitored on a continuing basis, though none currently viewed as threatening the Company's existence.
